words.tr: n. 殖民者；殖民地居民；移民
words.ex: The colonist built a small house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位殖民者在河边建了一座小房子。
words.en: A colonist is a person who settles in a new colony or moves to live in a new country.

words.ex: The car consumes a lot of gas.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车消耗很多汽油。
words.en: To consume something means to eat or drink it, or to use it up in some way.

words.tr: adj. 有人居住的；人口密集的； v. 居住于；“populate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The island is populated by only a few families.
words.ex_cn: 这个岛上只有几户人家居住。
words.en: An area that is populated has people living there.

words.tr: adj. 搞错的；弄错的；误解的； v. “mistake”的过去分词；
words.ex: He was mistaken about the time of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他对会议的时间搞错了。
words.en: If you are mistaken about something, you are wrong about it.

words.tr: adv. 温顺地，逆来顺受地
words.ex: She accepted the criticism meekly.
words.ex_cn: 她温顺地接受了批评。
words.en: In a meek manner; submissively.

words.ex: The rebellion against the king failed.
words.ex_cn: 反对国王的叛乱失败了。
words.en: A rebellion is an organized attempt to overthrow a government or authority by a group of people.

words.ex: He worked hard, and ultimately succeeded.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，最终成功了。
words.en: You use ultimately to indicate that something is the final result of a series of events or the most important part of a situation.

words.tr: phrase. 朝…方向前进；向…走去；努力接近（某目标）
words.ex: He make one's way towards the door.
words.ex_cn: 他向门口走去。
words.en: To move or travel in the direction of a particular place.

words.ex: The boat stops at the wharf near the sea.
words.ex_cn: 船停在海边的码头。
words.en: A wharf is a platform built out into the water where ships can be tied up and goods can be loaded or unloaded.

words.tr: phrase. 掌握；控制；指挥（尤指军队或组织）
words.ex: He takes command of the team during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中指挥这支队伍。
words.en: To assume control or authority over a group, organization, or situation.

words.ex: He woke up early for the purpose of catching the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他早起是为了赶公交车。
words.en: If you do something for the purpose of achieving a particular result, you do it in order to achieve that result.

words.ex: The bird hatched her eggs after three weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟在三周后孵出了她的蛋。
words.en: To hatch means to cause an egg to break open so that a young animal can come out, or to plan secretly with other people to do something bad or illegal.

words.tr:
n. 损害；破损；
v. 损害；破坏；
words.ex: The storm caused serious damage to the house.
words.ex_cn: 风暴对房屋造成了严重损害。
words.en: Damage is physical harm that is caused to something which makes it less attractive, useful, or valuable.

words.ex: He rubbed his chest after the cough.
words.ex_cn: 他咳嗽后揉了揉胸部。
words.en: The front part of a person's body between the neck and the stomach, or a large strong box used for storing things.

words.tr:
v. 分开；分裂；
n. 划分；分歧；
words.ex: The tree split in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那棵树在风暴中裂开了。
words.en: If something splits or if you split it, it is divided into two or more parts.

words.tr: phrase. 一接触到…；与…接触时
words.ex: The alarm goes off on contact with the intruder.
words.ex_cn: 警报器一接触到入侵者就会响起。
words.en: At the moment of touching or meeting something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 大量的；大批的；许多的
words.ex: He bought large quantities of rice for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为聚会买了大量的大米。
words.en: A large amount or number of something.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.tr:
n. 主题；学科；对象；
v. 使臣服；
adj. 易遭受…的；受…支配的；
words.ex: The subject of the book is ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的主题是古代历史。
words.en: A subject is something that is discussed, studied, or written about. It can also refer to a person or thing that is the focus of attention or action. In grammar, a subject is the part of a sentence that performs the action of the verb.

words.tr: adj. 不满意的；不高兴的； v. “dissatisfy”的过去式；
words.ex: He was dissatisfied with the service.
words.ex_cn: 他对服务不满意。
words.en: If you are dissatisfied with something, you are not contented or pleased with it.

words.ex: The old house has a colonial style.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子具有殖民地风格。
words.en: Colonial means relating to a system or period of colonization, or to the people who live in a colony.

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful representation of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是对自然的美丽表现。
words.en: A representation of something is a picture, a model of it, or a description of it that you create or that someone else creates for you.

words.ex: He worked extra hours to make up for the lost time.
words.ex_cn: 他加班工作来弥补失去的时间。
words.en: To compensate for something that is lacking or has been lost.

words.tr: phrase. 愿意做某事的；准备好做某事的
words.ex_cn: 他准备好为自己的目标努力工作。
words.en: To be ready and willing to do something.

words.tr: phrase. 屈服于；向…让步；投降
words.ex: Don't give in to fear when you face a challenge.
words.ex_cn: 当你面对挑战时，不要向恐惧屈服。
words.en: To yield to someone or something, especially after resisting for a period of time.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: The noise was intolerable.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音无法忍受。
words.en: If you describe something as intolerable, you mean that it is so bad or extreme that no one can bear it or tolerate it.

words.ex: He is a signatory to the peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 他是和平条约的签署方。
words.en: A signatory is a person, organization, or country that has signed an official document, especially a treaty or agreement.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.ex: He is a silversmith who makes beautiful rings.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位制作精美戒指的银匠。
words.en: A silversmith is a craftsman who makes objects out of silver.

words.ex: He is a true patriot who loves his country.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位真正热爱祖国的爱国者。
words.en: A patriot is someone who loves their country and is willing to defend it against enemies or detractors.

words.tr: n. 爱国主义；爱国精神；
words.ex: He showed patriotism by serving his country in the army.
words.ex_cn: 他通过在军队中为国家服务表现出爱国主义。
words.en: Patriotism is the love and devotion to one's country.

words.ex: The craftsman made a wooden chair by hand.
words.ex_cn: 这位工匠手工制作了一把木椅。
words.en: A craftsman is a skilled worker who makes things by hand.

words.tr:
adj. 军事的；军用的；
n. 军队；武装力量；
words.ex: The military base is near the border.
words.ex_cn: 军事基地靠近边境。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces

words.ex: The students sat in a row.
words.ex_cn: 学生们坐成一排。
words.en: A row is a straight line of things or people. To row means to move a boat through water using oars.

words.ex: The sentry stands guard at the gate.
words.ex_cn: 哨兵站在门口站岗。
words.en: A sentry is a soldier stationed at a place to stand guard and prevent surprise attacks.

words.tr:
adj. 有规律的；经常的；常见的；
n. 常客；
words.ex: He goes for a run every morning, a regular habit.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跑步，这是一个有规律的习惯。
words.en: Something that is regular happens or is done at equal intervals or is consistent in pattern or occurrence.

words.tr:
n. 巡逻
v. 巡逻
words.ex: The police patrol the street at night.
words.ex_cn: 警察晚上在街上巡逻。
words.en: A patrol is a group of soldiers or vehicles that are guarding a place at a particular time. Patrol can also refer to the act of moving around an area or building at regular times to check that it is safe.

words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.tr: phrase. 随意篡改；擅自改动；对…不拘礼节（常含贬义）
words.ex: He takes liberties with the rules to help his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他为了帮助朋友而随意违反规则。
words.en: To make changes to something in a way that is not strictly accurate or respectful, often adding one's own ideas or interpretations.

words.tr:
n. 信用；赊账；赞扬；贷款；荣誉；
v. 相信；
words.ex: He has good credit with the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他在银行有良好的信用。
words.en: If you are allowed credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.tr: phrase. v. 描述；说明；叙述某事的经过或情况
words.ex: Please give an account of what happened yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 请描述一下昨天发生的事情。
words.en: To provide a detailed description or explanation of something.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.ex: He endow a library with books.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一图书馆的书。
words.en: If someone is endowed with a particular quality or ability, they naturally have it.

words.tr: adj. 不可转让; （指权利等）不能让与的，不能剥夺的
words.ex: The right to life is unalienable.
words.ex_cn: 生存权是不可剥夺的。
words.en: If you say that something is unalienable, you mean that it cannot be taken away from you or denied.

words.ex: The coup led to the usurpation of power by the military.
words.ex_cn: 政变导致军事力量篡夺了政权。
words.en: The act of taking someone's position or power illegally or by force.

words.ex: The people rose up against the tyranny of the king.
words.ex_cn: 人民反抗了国王的暴虐。
words.en: Tyranny is cruel and unfair treatment by someone with power over other people, or a government in which a single ruler has absolute power.

words.tr: adv. 严肃地；庄严地；郑重地
words.ex: The judge solemnly swore to uphold the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官庄严宣誓要维护法律。
words.en: In a manner that is serious, formal, and dignified.

words.ex: The tyrant ruled the country with fear.
words.ex_cn: 暴君用恐惧统治国家。
words.en: A tyrant is a ruler who has complete power in a country and uses it in a cruel and unfair way.

words.ex: He filed a grievance about the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因不公平的对待提出了不满。
words.en: A grievance is a feeling of resentment over something believed to be wrong or unfair.

words.ex: The abolition of slavery took many years.
words.ex_cn: 废除奴隶制花了许多年。
words.en: The act of officially ending or stopping something, such as a system, practice, or institution.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: This rule is applicable to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If something is applicable to a particular situation, it is relevant or suitable for that situation.

words.ex: His sensitivity to loud noises makes him wear earplugs.
words.ex_cn: 他对噪音的敏感性让他戴耳塞。
words.en: Sensitivity is the quality or condition of being sensitive—the capacity to respond to slight changes, signals, or influences.

words.tr:
v. 集中；聚焦；
n. 中心点；焦点；
words.ex: He needs to focus on his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他需要集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you focus on a particular topic or if your attention is focused on it, you concentrate on it and think about it, discuss it, or deal with it, rather than dealing with other topics.

words.tr: adj. 统治的；支配的； v. “rule”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ruling class controls the government.
words.ex_cn: 统治阶级控制着政府。
words.en: A ruling is an official decision made by a judge or court, or a decision made by someone in authority.

words.ex: He will enroll in the English course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将注册英语课程。
words.en: To officially register or enlist oneself or someone else in a course, institution, or organization.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.ex: The mob broke the windows and shouted loudly.
words.ex_cn: 乌合之众砸了窗户并大声喊叫。
words.en: A mob is a large crowd of people, especially one that is disorderly and intent on causing trouble or violence.

words.ex: He smashed the glass with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把玻璃打碎了。
words.en: To break something into pieces violently and noisily, or to cause something to do this by dropping, throwing, or hitting it.

words.ex: The integration of technology and education improves learning.
words.ex_cn: 技术与教育的结合改善了学习。
words.en: The act or process of combining or adding parts to make a unified whole.

words.tr: phrase. 在逃；匆忙地；奔波；不停地移动
words.ex: He has been on the run since the bank heist.
words.ex_cn: 自从银行抢劫案以来，他一直在逃亡。
words.en: If someone is on the run, they are trying to avoid being captured by the police, often by moving from place to place.

words.ex: He faced imprisonment for stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷钱而面临监禁。
words.en: The state of being confined in prison; the act of putting someone in prison or the condition of being kept in prison.

words.tr: n. （以往南非的）种族隔离制度
words.ex: He lived under apartheid in South Africa.
words.ex_cn: 他在南非生活在种族隔离制度下。
words.en: A policy or system of segregation or discrimination on grounds of race, especially the policy that was in place in South Africa from 1948 to 1994.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.tr:
n. 亡命之徒；逃犯；被剥夺法律权益者
v. 宣布…为非法；使…成为非法
words.ex: The police caught the outlaw last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓住了那个不法之徒。
words.en: An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and who is hiding or running away to avoid punishment. To outlaw something means to make it illegal.

words.ex: They pave the road with stones.
words.ex_cn: 他们用石头铺路。
words.en: To cover a piece of ground with a hard, flat surface of pieces of stone, concrete, etc.

words.tr:
n. 火花；火星；
v. 激发；
words.ex: The match produced a small spark.
words.ex_cn: 火柴产生了一个小火花。
words.en: A spark is a small fiery particle thrown off from a fire, alight in ashes, or produced by striking together two hard surfaces such as stone or metal.

words.ex: The boy showed defiance by refusing to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 男孩通过拒绝遵守规则来表现违抗。
words.en: Defiance is behaviour or an attitude which shows that you are not willing to obey someone or something.

words.tr: n. 隔离；分离；种族隔离；
words.ex: The school practiced racial segregation in the past.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去实行种族隔离。
words.en: Segregation is the policy or practice of separating people of different races, sexes, or religions and treating them in a different way.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: She worked as a seamstress in a small tailor's shop.
words.ex_cn: 她在一家小裁缝店里做女裁缝。
words.en: A woman whose occupation is sewing, especially one who sews professionally.

words.ex: He was sent to jail for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窃被送进了监狱。
words.en: A place where people are kept as a punishment for a crime they have committed, or while they are waiting to go to court for their trial.

words.tr: adj. 不可估量的；不可测量的；无限的
words.ex: The love between them is immeasurable.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的爱是无法衡量的。
words.en: If you describe something as immeasurable, you are emphasizing that it is extremely great in size or degree.

words.tr:
n. 抵制；拒绝参加；
v. 抵制；拒绝参加；
words.ex: The students organized a boycott of the unfair school rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们组织了对这项不公平校规的抵制。
words.en: If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.

words.ex: Birds are inherently able to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类固有地能够飞行。
words.en: In a way that is a natural or essential part of something.

words.tr: v. 到达…的顶点；达到高潮；告终
words.ex: The concert culminated with a loud fireworks show.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会以一场响亮的烟花表演结束。
words.en: If an event or series of events culminates in something, it ends with it, having developed until it reaches this point.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: The infliction of pain is illegal.
words.ex_cn: 施加痛苦是非法的。
words.en: The act of imposing something unpleasant or painful on someone or something.

words.ex: The war showed the inhumanity of violence.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争展现了暴力的非人性。
words.en: The quality of lacking compassion or kindness; cruelty.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.tr:
n. 形状；身材；定形；
v. 塑造；
words.ex: The shape of the table is round.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子的形状是圆形的。
words.en: The shape of an object is its external form or outline, which can be seen and felt.

words.tr: adj. 有帮助的；乐器的；仪器的；
words.ex: Her advice was instrumental in helping me pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对帮助我通过考试很有帮助。
words.en: If someone or something is instrumental in a process, plan, or system, they are one of the most important influences in causing it to happen.

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.tr: adj. 说不出口的；无法形容的；不可说的
words.ex: The atrocities committed were unspeakable.
words.ex_cn: 所犯下的暴行是无法形容的。
words.en: If you describe something as unspeakable, you are emphasizing that it is extremely unpleasant or bad.

words.ex: The flaw in the glass made it break easily.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃上的瑕疵让它很容易碎。
words.en: A flaw is a mistake or weakness in something that makes it less effective or valuable.

words.ex: He felt shame for lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对母亲撒谎而感到羞愧。
words.en: A painful feeling of humiliation or distress caused by the consciousness of wrong or foolish behavior.

words.tr:
n. 根；根源；
v. 生根；
words.ex: The root of 9 is 3.
words.ex_cn: 9的平方根是3。
words.en: The root of a plant is the part that grows underground and absorbs water and minerals. It can also refer to the origin or cause of something.

words.ex: His creed is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A creed is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way people live or work.

words.ex: The children were exposed to cold weather without coats.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在没有外套的情况下遭受了寒冷天气。
words.en: To expose something means to uncover it so that it can be seen, or to make it known or public.

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.tr: n. 住处；膳宿；(交通工具内的)空间；
words.ex: The hotel provided cheap accommodation for travelers.
words.ex_cn: 酒店为旅客提供了便宜的住处。
words.en: Accommodation is a place where someone lives or stays, or the act of providing someone with a place to live or stay.

words.tr: n. 损失；伤亡人数；通行费；
words.ex: The war caused a heavy toll on innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 战争给平民带来了巨大的损失。
words.en: A toll is a small sum of money that you have to pay in order to use a particular bridge or road. / A toll is the total number of deaths, accidents, or disasters that occur in a particular period of time. / When a bell tolls, it rings slowly and repeatedly, often as a sign that someone has died.

words.tr: phrase. 使充气；爆炸；发怒；夸大
words.ex: He blew up the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他用嘴把气球吹鼓了。
words.en: If someone blows something up or if it blows up, it is destroyed by an explosion.

words.tr: adj. 不愿意的；不情愿的；
words.ex: He was unwilling to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意帮助他的朋友。
words.en: If you are unwilling to do something, you do not want to do it and will not agree to do it.

words.tr: n. 西洋菜；豆瓣菜；水田芥
words.ex: Watercress is often used in salads for its peppery flavor.
words.ex_cn: 豆瓣菜常用于沙拉中，因其胡椒味而受欢迎。
words.en: Watercress is a small, leafy plant that grows in water and is often used in salads or as a garnish.

words.ex: She ate a crisp apple for snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一个脆苹果当点心。
words.en: Something that is crisp is hard, and makes a pleasant sound when you break it or crush it.

words.tr: adj. 辛辣的；胡椒味的；暴躁的
words.ex: The soup has a peppery taste.
words.ex_cn: 这汤有辛辣的味道。
words.en: Having the hot, spicy flavor of pepper; easily irritated or angered.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.ex: He kneel to pray every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跪下祈祷。
words.en: To kneel means to go down into a position where one or both knees are on the ground.

words.tr: adj. 较低的；下游的；“low”的比较级； v. 降低；
words.ex: He sat in the lower row of the theater.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在剧院的较低一排。
words.en: If you lower something, you move it slowly downwards. If you lower something, you make it less in amount, degree, value, or quality.

words.ex: The cat sat on the ledge of the window.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在窗户的架状突出物上。
words.en: A ledge is a narrow horizontal surface projecting from a wall, cliff, or other surface.

words.tr: n. 工作服；罩衫；宽松式衬衫
words.ex: The painter wore a smock to protect his clothes.
words.ex_cn: 画家穿了一件工作服来保护他的衣服。
words.en: A smock is a loose garment worn over clothes to protect them while working or doing messy tasks.

words.ex: The soldier carries a carbine in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵在森林里携带一支卡宾枪。
words.en: A carbine is a short-barreled rifle, often used by cavalry and mounted infantry.

words.tr:
v. 吊起；悬挂；投掷
n. 投掷；悬带
words.ex: The nurse slung the arm in a bandage.
words.ex_cn: 护士用绷带吊起手臂。
words.en: To throw or hurl something with force; to suspend or hang something loosely.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 站起来；恢复过来（尤指经历困难后重新振作）
words.ex: After the fall, he tried to get to his feet.
words.ex_cn: 摔倒后，他试图站起来。
words.en: To stand up, especially after sitting or lying down.

words.ex: He grudgingly agreed to help.
words.ex_cn: 他勉强同意帮忙。
words.en: If you do something grudgingly, you do it unwillingly, often because you feel that you have to do it.

words.ex: He wore a big grin after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后露出了灿烂的咧嘴笑容。
words.en: If you grin, you smile broadly, usually showing your teeth.

words.tr:
v. 拍动；摆动；
n. 薄片；
words.ex: The bird flaps its wings to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟拍动翅膀飞翔。
words.en: A flap is a piece of cloth, paper, skin etc that is fixed at one edge to a surface, which you can lift up easily. If something such as a piece of cloth or paper flaps or if you flap it, it moves quickly up and down or from side to side.

words.ex: He wears a flannel shirt in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天穿法兰绒衬衫。
words.en: Flannel is a soft woven fabric, typically made of wool or cotton and slightly napped on one or both sides.

words.tr: adv. 不高兴地，绷着脸，忧郁地
words.ex: She responded sullenly to his question.
words.ex_cn: 她绷着脸回答他的问题。
words.en: In a manner that shows irritation or ill humor by a gloomy silence or reserve.

words.ex: The workers used dynamite to break the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 工人们使用炸药来炸开岩石。
words.en: Dynamite is a type of explosive that is used in mining and construction. It is also used metaphorically to describe something that is highly effective or potentially dangerous.

words.ex: Paint the wall evenly.
words.ex_cn: 均匀地刷墙。
words.en: In a manner that is equal, uniform, or balanced.

words.tr:
n. 袋子；
v. 劫掠；
words.ex: He carried the apples in a burlap sack.
words.ex_cn: 他把苹果装在一个麻布袋里。
words.en: A sack is a large bag made of rough woven material, used for storing or carrying goods. It can also refer to the act of dismissing someone from employment or the act of looting a place.

words.ex: The old man looked gaunt after his illness.
words.ex_cn: 这场病后，老人显得消瘦。
words.en: If someone looks gaunt, they look very thin, usually because they have been ill or worried.

words.tr:
n. 折痕；皱痕
v. 起皱；弄皱
words.ex: The paper has a deep crease from folding.
words.ex_cn: 这张纸因为折叠而有一道深深的折痕。
words.en: A crease is a line or mark made on cloth or paper when it is folded or crushed.

words.ex: Water causes erosion of the soil.
words.ex_cn: 水会导致土壤腐蚀。
words.en: The process by which the surface of the earth is worn away by the action of water, glaciers, winds, waves, etc.

words.ex: The marlin is a prized catch for many sport fishermen.
words.ex_cn: 枪鱼是许多运动渔民梦寐以求的捕获物。
words.en: A marlin is a large, long-nosed marine fish that is highly prized by anglers for its size and fighting spirit when hooked.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.ex: This room is relatively small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间相对较小。
words.en: In comparison with other similar things or with what you expect.

words.tr: adv. 显然；表面上看起来；
words.ex: He is apparently late for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他显然迟到了会议。
words.en: You use apparently to indicate that the information you are giving is something that you have heard, but you are not certain that it is true.

words.ex: The mechanic fixed my car quickly.
words.ex_cn: 机修工很快修好了我的车。
words.en: A mechanic is a person whose job is to repair and maintain machines and engines, especially those of vehicles.

words.tr: adv. 似乎；看似；表面上看；
words.ex: He is seemingly calm, but he is nervous inside.
words.ex_cn: 他似乎很平静，但内心很紧张。
words.en: appearing to be true or real but not necessarily so

words.ex: The ticket is invalid because it expired.
words.ex_cn: 这张票无效，因为它已经过期了。
words.en: If something is invalid, it is not legally or officially acceptable, or it is not based on truth or reason.

words.tr: adj. 愤世嫉俗的；悲观的；
words.ex: He gave a cynical smile when they talked about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 当他们谈到诚实时，他露出了愤世嫉俗的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as cynical, you mean they believe that people always act selfishly.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.ex: He spoke distinctly so everyone could understand.
words.ex_cn: 他说话很清晰，以便每个人都能听懂。
words.en: In a way that is clear and unmistakable.

words.tr: adj. 关于花的；花饰的；过分华丽的；虚饰的
words.ex: Her speech was full of flowery phrases.
words.ex_cn: 她的演讲充满了华丽的辞藻。
words.en: Something that is flowery is full of elaborate or literary words and phrases.

words.ex: The village has a sparse population.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄人口稀少。
words.en: Something that is sparse is small in number or amount and spread out over an area.

words.ex: He writes simple prose every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天写简单的散文。
words.en: Prose is written language in its ordinary form, without metrical structure.

words.tr: phrase. 省去； 遗漏； 不考虑
words.ex: Don't leave out the sugar in the recipe.
words.ex_cn: 别在食谱里漏掉糖。
words.en: To not include someone or something in an activity or discussion.

words.tr: adj. 革新的；富有革新精神的；
words.ex: The company made an innovative phone.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司推出了一款革新的手机。
words.en: Something that is innovative is new and original, especially in the way that it is done.

words.ex: The cloud floats high in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 云朵在天空中飘浮。
words.en: A cloud is a visible mass of condensed water vapor floating in the atmosphere, typically high above the ground.

words.ex: The lighthouse stands on a promontory overlooking the sea.
words.ex_cn: 灯塔建在俯瞰大海的岬角上。
words.en: A promontory is a high point of land or rock projecting into a body of water; a headland.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.tr:
n. 管子；管道；烟斗；
v. 吹笛；以管输送；
words.ex: The plumber fixed the broken pipe.
words.ex_cn: 水管工修好了坏掉的管子。
words.en: A pipe is a long, round, hollow object, usually made of metal or plastic, through which a liquid or gas can flow.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.tr:
n. 猎犬
v. 追逐；纠缠
words.ex: The hound chased the rabbit through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎犬在森林里追赶兔子。
words.en: A hound is a type of dog used for hunting or chasing. It can also refer to someone who persistently pursues or bothers someone else.

words.tr: n. 伪造；伪造罪；伪造物
words.ex: He was arrested for forgery.
words.ex_cn: 他因伪造被逮捕了。
words.en: Forgery is the crime of making or altering a document or signature with the intent to deceive or defraud.

words.tr:
n. 服务人员
adj. 随之而来的
words.ex: The attendant helped me find my seat.
words.ex_cn: 服务员帮我找到了座位。
words.en: An attendant is someone whose job is to serve or help people in a public place.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的；
words.ex: He made a shrewd decision to buy the house low.
words.ex_cn: 他精明地决定低价买下这栋房子。
words.en: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏想象力的；无趣的
words.ex: He gave an unimaginative answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个缺乏创意的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimaginative, you are criticizing them because they do not think of new or interesting ideas or things.

words.ex: She decided to stretch out on the beach and enjoy the sun.
words.ex_cn: 她决定在沙滩上伸展身体，享受阳光。
words.en: To extend or lengthen one's body or a part of one's body to its full length.

words.ex: He used a roller to flatten the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 他用滚筒把泥土压平。
words.en: To flatten something means to make it flat or flatter, or to knock it down to the ground.

words.ex: The dark clouds are an indication of rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是下雨的迹象。
words.en: An indication is a sign which suggests, for example, what people are thinking or feeling.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；涂写
n. 潦草的笔迹
words.ex: He scrawled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了自己的名字。
words.en: If you scrawl something, you write it in a careless and untidy way.

words.ex: The legend says a dragon lives in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 传说有一条龙住在山里。
words.en: A legend is a very old and popular story that may be true or may be imaginary.

words.ex: He will consult a doctor for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他将咨询医生治疗他的头痛。
words.en: to seek information or advice from someone, especially someone who is an expert in a particular field

words.ex: The house is connected to the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子连接到供水系统。
words.en: To be joined or linked to something else, allowing communication or passage between them.

words.tr:
adj. 精瘦的；精简的；不景气的；
v. 倾斜；倚靠；
words.ex: The dog is lean and fast.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗精瘦而敏捷。
words.en: If you lean in a particular direction, you bend your body in that direction. If you lean on or against someone or something, you rest against them so that they partly support your weight. If you describe someone as lean, you mean that they are thin but look strong and healthy. If you describe a period of time as lean, you mean that it is a time when people have very little of something, especially money.

words.tr: prep. 关于； v. “concern”的现在分词；
words.ex: The book is concerning climate change.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于气候变化的。
words.en: If something is concerning, it causes you to feel concerned about it.

words.tr:
n. 旷野地；荒野；高沼
v. （使）停泊；系泊
words.ex: The sheep graze on the moor near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊在村庄附近的旷野地上吃草。
words.en: A moor is an area of open land, often with poor soil, that is covered with grass, heather, and low bushes. It can also refer to the act of securing a ship or boat to a fixed object or the land.

words.tr: phrase. 有关系；和…连在一起
words.ex: This event is connected with the history of the city.
words.ex_cn: v. 这个事件与城市的历史有联系。
words.en: To be related to or associated with someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 因某事而称赞某人；承认某人的功劳
words.ex: You have to give him credit for his persistence.
words.ex_cn: 你必须为他的坚持不懈而赞扬他。
words.en: To acknowledge or praise someone for something they have done.

words.ex: Mom reassured me that everything would be fine.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈让我安心，一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you reassure someone, you comfort them and stop them from worrying.

words.ex: He has an insatiable hunger for knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识有着无法满足的渴望。
words.en: If someone is insatiable, they always want more of something and are never satisfied.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.tr: adj. 忠实的；虔诚的；可靠的；
words.ex: He is a faithful friend who always helps me.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是帮助我的忠实朋友。
words.en: Someone who is faithful remains loyal to a person, belief, or cause, and continues to support them.

words.tr:
n. 代用品；代替物；
v. 替代；
words.ex: Honey is a good substitute for sugar.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是糖的良好代用品。
words.en: A substitute is something or someone that takes the place or function of another.

words.ex: This movie is a horror genre film.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部恐怖类型影片。
words.en: A genre is a particular type of literature, painting, music, film, or other art form which people consider as a class because it has special characteristics.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: The orange was squeezed into a sweet pulp.
words.ex_cn: 橙子被榨成了甜美的浆状物。
words.en: The soft, wet, shapeless mass of material that is left after the juice has been removed from fruit or vegetables, or the soft inner part of a tooth.

words.ex: He is viewed as a good teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他被视为一位好老师。
words.en: To be considered or regarded in a particular way.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的；引人入胜的； v. “intrigue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mystery story was intriguing.
words.ex_cn: 这个侦探故事很引人入胜。
words.en: If you describe something as intriguing, you mean that it is interesting or strange.

words.ex: The old manor stood beside a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的庄园坐落在一个大湖旁边。
words.en: A large country house with lands; the principal house of a landed estate.

words.ex: The small room was cosy with a warm blanket and a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间铺着温暖的毯子，喝着热茶，非常舒适。
words.en: A place or situation that is cosy is comfortable and warm.

words.tr: adj. 不切实际的；不实事求是的；
words.ex: It's unrealistic to expect to get rich quickly.
words.ex_cn: 指望快速致富是不切实际的。
words.en: If you say that someone is being unrealistic, you mean that they do not recognize the truth about a situation, especially about the difficulties involved in something they want to achieve.

words.tr: phrase. 相比之下；和...形成对照
words.ex: He likes coffee, in contrast to his sister who likes tea.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢咖啡，而他的妹妹喜欢茶。
words.en: used when you are comparing two things or people and saying that the second one is very different from the first

words.ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕太阳转。
words.en: If something revolves or if you revolve something, it moves or turns around a central point or line.

words.tr:
n. （鸟或羊）群；（人）群；
v. 聚集；群集；
words.ex: A flock of birds flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过田野。
words.en: A flock is a group of birds, sheep, or goats, or a large group of people. It can also refer to a soft material for stuffing cushions, quilts, etc., made from wool or cotton. As a verb, it means to gather or move in a flock.

words.tr: n. 公共卫生；卫生设施；
words.ex: The city improved sanitation to keep people healthy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了公共卫生以保障人民健康。
words.en: The conditions and processes that help maintain health and prevent disease, especially through cleanliness.

words.ex: The dog is a scavenger and eats leftover food.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗是拾荒者，吃剩下的食物。
words.en: A scavenger is an animal that feeds on dead organisms, especially a carnivorous animal that eats dead animals rather than or in addition to hunting live prey.

words.ex: The city cleaned the sewage from the streets.
words.ex_cn: 城市清理了街道上的污水。
words.en: Sewage is waste matter such as faeces or dirty water from homes and factories, which flows away through sewers.

words.tr:
v. 实施；传导（电、热）；
n. 行为；举止；
words.ex: The company will conduct a survey next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周进行一项调查。
words.en: To organize and carry out a particular activity.

words.ex: He earned his doctorate in biology.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了生物学博士学位。
words.en: A doctorate is the highest level of academic degree awarded by universities, following the completion of a course of study demonstrating the ability to conduct independent research.

words.ex: The test uses psychometric scales to measure anxiety.
words.ex_cn: 这个测试使用心理测量量表来测量焦虑。
words.en: Psychometric refers to the measurement of mental capacities and processes, especially through the use of psychological tests.

words.tr:
n. 规模；等级；比例（尺）；刻度；秤；
v. 改变…大小；
words.ex: The scale of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的规模让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.

words.ex: The aggression of the army caused many deaths.
words.ex_cn: 军队的侵略导致了许多人死亡。
words.en: Aggression is a violent or hostile behavior towards another person or country.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.ex: The body has a mechanism to fight viruses.
words.ex_cn: 人体有一种对抗病毒的机制。
words.en: A mechanism is a part of a machine that does a particular task, or a system that is intended to achieve something or deal with a problem.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.tr: adj. 不合适的；不相称的；不协调的；
words.ex: His funny hat was incongruous with the formal suit.
words.ex_cn: 他的滑稽帽子与正式西装不搭配。
words.en: Something that is incongruous is strange when considered together with other aspects of a situation.

words.ex: His familiarity with the city helped him find the way.
words.ex_cn: 他对这座城市的熟悉帮助他找到了路。
words.en: A thorough knowledge or mastery of a subject, place, or situation, often gained through experience.

words.tr: phrase. 更确切地说；倒不如说
words.ex: He is not lazy, or rather, he is efficient in his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他并不懒，或者更准确地说，他有自己的高效方式。
words.en: used to correct or modify what has just been said, or to say it more accurately

words.ex: The outcome of the game was a tie.
words.ex_cn: 比赛的结果是平局。
words.en: The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.

words.tr:
n. 双关语
v. 说双关语
words.ex: He made a bad pun and everyone groaned.
words.ex_cn: 他开了个蹩脚的玩笑，大家都皱起了眉头。
words.en: A pun is a clever and amusing use of a word or phrase with two meanings, or of words with the same sound but different meanings.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.ex: The pink hat on the man looked like an incongruity.
words.ex_cn: 男人头上的粉红色帽子显得很不协调。
words.en: The state of being incongruous; incompatibility.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.tr: adj. 分离的； v. 脱离；拆卸；分离；“detach”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is detached from the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子与邻居的房子是分开的。
words.en: If someone is detached, they do not have any emotional interest in a situation and therefore can make fair decisions.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.ex: The limitation of the phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的限制是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A limitation is a rule or situation that restricts what you can do or what can happen.

words.tr:
n. 寓言；神话传说；无稽之谈
v. 虚构
words.ex: The old man told a fable about a fox and a crow.
words.ex_cn: 老人讲了一个关于狐狸和乌鸦的寓言。
words.en: A fable is a short story that typically features animals as characters and conveys a moral lesson.

words.tr: phrase. v. 处理；安排；照料（某事）
words.ex: I will see about the meeting time.
words.ex_cn: 我会去确认一下会议时间。
words.en: To attend to or deal with something.

words.ex: I can count on my brother to help me.
words.ex_cn: 我可以依靠我哥哥帮我。
words.en: If you count on someone or something, you rely on them to support you or help you.

words.tr: adj. 狂暴的；骚动的；动荡的；汹涌的
words.ex: The turbulent sea made the boat shake.
words.ex_cn: 汹涌的海让船摇晃。
words.en: A turbulent situation, time, or relationship is one in which there is a lot of change, confusion, and often conflict.

words.tr: n. 暗示；提示；有益的建议；
words.ex: He gave me a hint about the surprise party.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我关于惊喜派对的暗示。
words.en: A hint is a slight or indirect indication or suggestion.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.tr:
n. 懦夫；胆小鬼；胆怯者
adj. 胆小的；怯懦的
words.ex: He was a coward and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他是个懦夫，逃跑了。
words.en: A coward is someone who is easily frightened and avoids dangerous or difficult situations.

words.tr:
n. 地址；演讲；
v. 解决；向…讲话；
words.ex: Please write your address on the form.
words.ex_cn: 请把你的地址写在表格上。
words.en: The particulars of the place where someone lives or an organization is situated; a formal speech delivered to an audience.

words.ex: There is a resemblance between the two brothers.
words.ex_cn: 这两兄弟之间有相似之处。
words.en: If there is a resemblance between two people or things, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.tr: v. 讨好；“flatter”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt flattered when she praised his cooking.
words.ex_cn: 当她称赞他的厨艺时，他感到被讨好了。
words.en: If you are flattered by something that has happened or been said, you are pleased because it makes you feel important or special.

words.tr: 短语. 瞬间；片刻；一瞬间
words.ex: She hesitated for an instant before answering.
words.ex_cn: 她在回答之前犹豫了片刻。
words.en: For a very brief period of time.

words.tr: adv. 热诚地，诚挚地，友善地
words.ex: He cordially invited his friends to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他诚挚地邀请朋友参加派对。
words.en: In a warm and friendly manner.

words.ex: He vaguely remembered the name.
words.ex_cn: 他模糊地记得这个名字。
words.en: If you describe something as vaguely, you mean that it is not clear, distinct, or definite.

words.ex: The tree has many branches.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树有许多分支。
words.en: A branch of a tree is one of its parts that grows out from its trunk. A branch of a business or organization is one of its offices or shops that are in different places.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.tr:
adj. 空白的；
n. 空白处；
words.ex: The paper had a blank space at the top.
words.ex_cn: 这张纸的顶部有一个空白区域。
words.en: If something is blank, it has nothing on it.

words.tr: adj. 令人烦恼的；讨厌的；
words.ex: The noisy neighbors are troublesome.
words.ex_cn: 那些吵闹的邻居令人烦恼。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as troublesome, you mean that they cause you a lot of problems or worries.

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.ex: After the break, we will proceed with the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 休息后，我们将继续开会。
words.en: If you proceed to do something, you continue to do it or start to do it after doing something else first.

words.tr:
n. 脸红；羞愧
v. 泛红；羞愧
words.ex: He felt shy and got a blush when she praised him.
words.ex_cn: 当他被她夸奖时，他感到害羞，脸红了。
words.en: If you blush, your face turns red because you are embarrassed or ashamed.

words.ex: He is presently working at a bank.
words.ex_cn: 他现在在一家银行工作。
words.en: At the present time; now. Or in a short time; soon.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.ex: He told an aphorism about patience.
words.ex_cn: 他说了一句关于耐心的格言。
words.en: An aphorism is a short, clever saying that expresses a general truth or observation.

words.ex: They will nominate her for the award.
words.ex_cn: 他们将提名她获得这个奖项。
words.en: If someone is nominated for a job or position, their name is formally suggested as a candidate for it.

words.ex: The bridge crosses the river.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥横跨河流。
words.en: A bridge is a structure that is built over a railway, river, or road so that people or vehicles can cross from one side to the other.

words.ex: Try to visualise a red ball floating in the air.
words.ex_cn: 试着想象一个红色的球在空中漂浮。
words.en: To form a mental image of; imagine.

words.ex: The teacher imbues her students with confidence.
words.ex_cn: 老师赋予学生信心。
words.en: If someone or something is imbued with a particular quality, feeling, or value, they are filled with it or characterized by it.

words.ex: The prevalence of flu increased in winter.
words.ex_cn: 流感在冬季更加流行。
words.en: The fact or condition of being prevalent; commonness.

words.ex: The painting showed a few small imperfections that the artist had missed.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画显示出艺术家忽略的几个小瑕疵。
words.en: An imperfection in something is a fault, weakness, or undesirable feature that it has.

words.ex: I perceive a change in his mood.
words.ex_cn: 我察觉到他的情绪有变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.ex: The children's laughter brought gaiety to the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们的笑声为派对带来了欢乐。
words.en: Gaiety is a feeling, attitude, or atmosphere of liveliness and fun.

words.ex: The difference between the two colors is subtle.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色之间的区别很微妙。
words.en: Something that is subtle is not immediately obvious or noticeable, but is rather indirect or understated.

words.ex: Mother's milk nourishes the baby.
words.ex_cn: 母乳滋养婴儿。
words.en: To nourish someone or something means to provide them with the food and other substances they need in order to live, grow, and be healthy.

words.ex: He dwells in a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一所小房子里。
words.en: If you dwell on something, especially something unpleasant, you think, speak, or write about it a lot or for quite a long time.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.ex: His words are a contradiction.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: A contradiction is a situation or statement in which two aspects or elements are opposed to each other, making it impossible for both to be true at the same time.

words.tr:
n. 弹跳；跳动；
v. 弹跳；反弹；
words.ex: The ball had a high bounce on the concrete.
words.ex_cn: 球在混凝土上弹跳得很高。
words.en: If something bounces or if you bounce it, it moves away from a surface after hitting it.

words.ex: The lightness of the box made it easy to carry.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的轻便让它很容易携带。
words.en: The quality of being light in weight or not heavy; the quality of being cheerful and carefree.

words.ex: The subtlety of her smile made everyone curious.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的微妙之处让所有人都感到好奇。
words.en: The quality of being subtle, especially in a way that is difficult to notice or understand.

words.tr:
n. 假象；假冒者；冒牌货
adj. 虚假的
v. 假装
words.ex: The gift was a sham, not real.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物是假的，不是真的。
words.en: A sham is something that is not what it appears to be and is intended to deceive people.

words.tr: n. 愚蠢；愚蠢行为；糊涂
words.ex: His stupidity made him fail the test.
words.ex_cn: 他的愚蠢让他考试不及格。
words.en: Stupidity is the quality of being stupid or lacking intelligence.

words.tr:
n. 欺诈；谎话；骗子
v. 欺骗；行骗
words.ex: He was accused of being a humbug and spreading false information.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控为骗子，散布虚假信息。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behaviour as humbug, you mean that it is dishonest or insincere.

words.ex: He gave a witty answer to the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师的问题给出了机智的回答。
words.en: Someone or something that is witty is amusing in a clever way.

words.tr: adj. 心智健全的；头脑清醒的；明智的
words.ex: He is still sane after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他仍然神志清醒。
words.en: If someone is sane, they are able to think and behave in a normal and rational manner.

words.ex: He burst into rage when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他勃然大怒。
words.en: Rage is a feeling of intense anger that is difficult to control.

words.ex: The universe came into existence billions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙在数十亿年前开始存在。
words.en: To begin to exist; to be created or formed.

words.tr: n. 总部；司令部；指挥部；
words.ex: The company's headquarters is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: The main office or center of control of a company, organization, or military unit.

words.ex: The Magna Carta is an old charter of rights.
words.ex_cn: 《大宪章》是一份古老的权力宪章。
words.en: A charter is a formal document describing the rights, aims, or principles of an organization or group of people.

words.ex: The resolution of the conflict took many meetings.
words.ex_cn: 这个冲突的解决花了多次会议。
words.en: A resolution is a formal decision made at a meeting by the vote of the people who are there. It can also refer to a firm decision to do or not to do something.

words.ex: The teacher gave me a recommendation for the scholarship.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我写了一封奖学金推荐信。
words.en: A suggestion or proposal as to the best course of action, especially one put forward by an authoritative body.

words.ex: The police enforce the law.
words.ex_cn: 警察强制执行法律。
words.en: If people in authority enforce a law or a rule, they make sure that it is obeyed, usually by punishing people who do not obey it.

words.ex: Please ensure the door is locked.
words.ex_cn: 请确保门锁好了。
words.en: To make certain that something will occur or be the case.

words.ex: He can eat one apple at a time.
words.ex_cn: 他一次只能吃一个苹果。
words.en: Indicates the number of items or actions that are involved in a single instance or occurrence.

words.tr:
n. 否决；否决权
v. 否决
words.ex: The president used his veto to stop the law.
words.ex_cn: 总统行使否决权阻止了这项法律。
words.en: If someone in authority vetoes something, they forbid it, or they stop it from being put into action.

words.ex: He made a proposal to improve the school lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个改善学校午餐的提案。
words.en: A proposal is a plan or suggestion, especially a formal one that is put forward for people to think about and decide upon.

words.tr: n. 外交官；会耍手腕儿的人
words.ex: The diplomat met the president yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 这位外交官昨天会见了总统。
words.en: A diplomat is a person who represents their country in a foreign country, managing political relations and negotiations.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.tr: v. 给予（药物或治疗）；管理；实施；
words.ex: The nurse will administer the medicine to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 护士会给病人服药。
words.en: To administer means to manage or oversee the execution, use, or conduct of something; to dispense or apply (a remedy or drug).

words.ex: The refugee walked to a new country.
words.ex_cn: 这名难民步行去了一个新国家。
words.en: A refugee is a person who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster.

words.ex: He wears a black beret every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天戴一顶黑色贝雷帽。
words.en: A beret is a round, flat hat made of soft material and has no brim.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.tr:
n. 冰雹；
v. 把…誉为；
words.ex: The hail broke many car windows.
words.ex_cn: 冰雹打碎了许多汽车窗户。
words.en: Hail is small balls of ice that fall like rain from the sky. It can also mean to call out to someone in order to attract their attention, or to praise someone enthusiastically.

words.tr: n. 伙伴关系；合作；合作关系；
words.ex: They formed a partnership to run a small shop.
words.ex_cn: 他们建立了一种伙伴关系来经营一家小店。
words.en: A partnership is a legal form of business operation between two or more individuals who share management and profits.

words.ex: His testimony proved the suspect was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他的证词证明了嫌疑人是无辜的。
words.en: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.ex: The disposal of waste is important for the environment.
words.ex_cn: 废物的处理对环境很重要。
words.en: The act or process of getting rid of something, especially by throwing it away or selling it.

words.ex: They plant trees to commemorate the fallen soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 他们种树以纪念阵亡的士兵。
words.en: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially created object.

words.tr:
n. 展示优点的场合（或机会）；
v. 展示…的优点；
words.ex: The competition was a showcase for her talent.
words.ex_cn: 这次比赛是她展示才华的机会。
words.en: A showcase is a setting in which someone or something is displayed to its best advantage, or a glass case used for displaying articles in a shop or museum.

words.ex: She coordinates the team's schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她协调团队的安排。
words.en: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it. If you coordinate the different parts of your body, you make them work together efficiently.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.ex: The pollution caused the degradation of the river.
words.ex_cn: 污染导致了河流的恶化。
words.en: The process by which something is reduced in quality, value, or status.

words.tr: n. 专题讨论会；研讨会
words.ex: He spoke at a symposium about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个关于气候变化的研讨会上发言。
words.en: A symposium is a conference or meeting to discuss a particular subject.

words.ex: Her smile heartened the tired students.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑鼓舞了疲惫的学生。
words.en: If someone is heartened by something, it encourages them and makes them cheerful.

words.tr:
v. 意思是说；表示…的意思；
n. 手段；方法；收入；
words.ex: This sign means you cannot park here.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志意思是说这里不能停车。
words.en: Means refers to a method or way of doing something, or the resources or assets available for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: The war led to the genocide of many innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争导致了众多无辜人民的种族灭绝。
words.en: Genocide is the deliberate killing of a large number of people from a particular nation or ethnic group with the aim of destroying that nation or group.

words.tr: adj. 可憎的；十恶不赦的
words.ex: He committed a heinous crime last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚犯下了一桩可怕的罪行。
words.en: If you describe something such as a crime as heinous, you mean that it is extremely evil or wicked.

words.tr: n. 秘书处；书记处；秘书（书记，部长等）的职位
words.ex: The secretariat sends out meeting notices every week.
words.ex_cn: 秘书处每周发送会议通知。
words.en: The administrative department of an organization, especially a large political organization, that is responsible for its day-to-day running.

words.ex: The proliferation of bacteria causes the infection to spread.
words.ex_cn: 细菌的增殖导致感染扩散。
words.en: The rapid increase in the number or amount of something.

words.tr: n. 裁减军备；解除武装；缴械
words.ex: The two countries agreed on disarmament to reduce weapons.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家同意进行裁军以减少武器。
words.en: The reduction or withdrawal of military forces and weapons.

words.tr:
n. 记号；分数；痕迹；
v. 做标记；（使）留痕迹；评分；
words.ex: He put a mark on the map to show the place.
words.ex_cn: 他在地图上做了一个记号来表示那个地方。
words.en: A mark is a small area or spot on a surface which is different in colour or texture from the area around it. If you mark something, you make a mark on it in order to identify it or to give information about it.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.tr:
n. 车费；费用；
v. 进展；成功（或不成功等）；
words.ex: The bus fare is two dollars.
words.ex_cn: 公交车费是两美元。
words.en: The fare is the amount of money that you pay for a journey that you make, for example, in a bus, train, or taxi.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.tr: adj. 多边的；多国参加的
words.ex: The multilateral agreement helped many countries work together.
words.ex_cn: 这个多边协议帮助许多国家共同合作。
words.en: Involving or agreed upon by three or more parties, especially the governments of different countries.

words.ex: The project is ongoing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.

words.ex: The transformation of the old factory into a park made the city nicer.
words.ex_cn: 把旧工厂改造成公园让城市变得更美了。
words.en: A transformation is a complete change in the appearance, form, or nature of something or someone.

words.ex: He gave a constructive comment on my essay.
words.ex_cn: 他对我的论文给出了建设性的评论。
words.en: If something is constructive, it is useful and intended to help or improve something.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.ex: The two teams showed synergy when they finished the project early.
words.ex_cn: 当这两个团队提前完成项目时，展现了协同效应。
words.en: The interaction or cooperation of two or more organizations, substances, or other agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their separate effects.

words.tr:
v. 预言；预测
n. （古罗马）占兆官；占卜师
words.ex: The early reviews augur well for the success of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 早期的评论预示着这部电影将取得成功。
words.en: to predict or foretell, especially from signs or omens

words.ex: Completing the project gave him a sense of fulfilment.
words.ex_cn: 完成这个项目给了他一种满足感。
words.en: Fulfilment refers to the achievement of something desired, promised, or predicted, or the satisfaction or happiness derived from this.

words.ex: The meeting was fruitful and solved many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议富有成效，解决了许多问题。
words.en: Producing good or helpful results; productive.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.ex: The baby was sleeping in the cradle.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在吊架里睡觉。
words.en: A cradle is a small bed for a baby, which can be rocked from side to side. It can also refer to the place or period in which something begins or is developed.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: He studies ecology to understand how animals live with plants.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生态学以了解动物如何与植物共存。
words.en: Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment; it seeks to understand the vital connections between plants and animals and the world around them.

words.ex: The rhinoceros walks slowly in the grass.
words.ex_cn: 犀牛在草地上慢慢行走。
words.en: A rhinoceros is a large, thick-skinned animal with one or two horns on its nose, native to Africa and southern Asia.

words.tr:
v. 保存；保护；保持；
n. （某群体）专有的活动；
words.ex: She preserves fresh fruit by making jam.
words.ex_cn: 她通过做果酱来保存新鲜水果。
words.en: To preserve something means to maintain it in its original or existing state.
